reference_title: Design and Construction of Continuous Flight Auger Piles
chapter_title: Guide Construction Specifications for Continuous Flight Auger (CFA) Piles

sections.title: Description and Submittals
sections.summary: Chapter 8 provides a performance-based guide specification for CFA piles. The contractor designs the piles to meet specified loading conditions using Chapter 5-6 ASD procedures, and verifies performance through load testing. Required submittals: design calculations and working drawings; pile installation plan (equipment, procedures, target drilling/grouting parameters); conformance testing plan. Contractor experience requirements must be documented. Geotechnical investigation report must be included in the contract special provisions as a legal document.
sections.body:
Definitions: CFA pile is any foundation made by rotating a hollow-stem auger to specified depth and injecting grout or concrete through the hollow stem as the auger is withdrawn. This specification is performance-based — the contractor is responsible for the pile design, subject to owner approval.

Contractor experience: The CFA pile contractor must provide documentation of a minimum experience requirement (to be filled in by owner). If subcontracted, the prime contractor must name the subcontractor sufficiently in advance for owner review.

CFA pile design requirements: Piles shall be designed using Service Load Design (SLD) per Chapters 5 and 6 of GEC-8. Design submittals include calculations covering: applicable code requirements; design cross-sections with soil strata, piezometric levels, and loads; design criteria (soil shear strengths, unit weights, unit skin friction and end-bearing values); pile layout plans and elevation views. Working drawings show pile locations and elevations.

Pile installation plan: Contractor must submit installation plan documenting equipment (rig type, torque capacity, crowd), auger type and size, grout/concrete mix design, target drilling and grouting parameters with acceptable ranges (rotation speed, penetration rates, torque, crowd pressure, grout pressure, grout volume factor), and automated monitoring system details. Right-of-way, utilities, and subsurface exploration locations must be shown on plan.

Conformance testing plan: Must identify pre-production test pile program requirements, and verification load tests and integrity tests for production piles. Test methods and frequencies per Sections 8.3.11 and 8.3.12.
key_points: Performance-based specification: contractor designs piles to meet specified loads and verifies by load tests
Contractor documents experience before work begins; subcontractor named in advance for owner review
Pile design per GEC-8 Chapters 5-6 (ASD); design submittals include calculations and working drawings
Pile installation plan: rig, auger, mix design, target parameters with ranges, automated monitoring description
Geotechnical investigation report included in contract special provisions as a legal document
sections.applicability: Submittal requirements for performance-based CFA pile construction contracts

sections.title: Construction Requirements
sections.summary: Key construction requirements: (1) unsuitable surface material within 1.5 m (5 ft) removed or treated; (2) monitor adjacent structures and stop immediately if movements detected; (3) grout/concrete placement within 5 minutes of reaching tip depth; (4) grout volume factor within 7.5% of target from pile installation plan; (5) adjacent piles within 6 diameters may not be installed until first pile has attained sufficient strength; (6) pile position tolerance: center within 75 mm (3 in.); (7) integrity testing on minimum 20% of production piles; (8) pre-production static load tests required; verification tests (static, RLT, or DLT) during production.
sections.body:
Site preparation: Remove muck, organics, soft clay, or other unsuitable materials within 1.5 m (5 ft) of grade. If movements are detected in adjacent structures, stop construction immediately, notify the engineer, and take remedial measures.

Grout/concrete requirements: Type I, II, or III Portland cement per ASTM C150. Fly ash Class C or F per ASTM C618. Water reducer/superplasticizer per ASTM C494. Grout fluidifier per ASTM C937. Grout: 50 mm (2 in.) cube samples for strength per ASTM C109; strength requirement typically 27.6–34.5 MPa (4,000–5,000 psi). Concrete: 150 mm (6 in.) cylinder samples per ASTM C39. Slump target 200 ± 25 mm (8 ± 1 in.) for concrete; grout workability measured by flow cone (modified 19 mm opening, efflux 10–25 sec).

Auger equipment: Auger flights must be continuous from top to bottom; gaps only at section joints, ≤25 mm (1 in.). Auger must reach design pile depth.

Automated monitoring: Required minimum automatic measurements every 2 ft (0.6 m) of pile: auger tip depth, grout/concrete volume, pump pressure at top of auger. Torque and crowd force may also be required during drilling. All measurements referenced to auger tip depth.

Drilling: Auger diameter, soil mining avoidance, penetration rate control per approved installation plan.

Grout/concrete placement: Placement must commence within 5 minutes of reaching planned depth. Grout/concrete must be pumped with sufficient pressure to completely form the pile. Volume factor must stay within 7.5% of target from the installation plan. If placement is suspended, pile must be abandoned and re-drilled.

Reinforcement placement: Placed by gravity into fluid grout/concrete. Non-metallic spacers only. Minimum cover 75 mm (3 in.) non-aggressive; 100 mm (4 in.) aggressive environments.

Pile position tolerance: Pile center within 75 mm (3 in.) of plan location. Plumb tolerance: deviation from vertical not to exceed specified angle.

Adjacent piles: Piles within 6 diameters center-to-center of each other shall not be installed until the first pile's grout/concrete has attained sufficient strength.

Testing: Pre-production static load tests required. Integrity tests on minimum 20% of production piles; methods include sonic echo (SE), impulse-response (IR), CSL, and gamma-gamma, per ASTM D5882 or D6760. Unacceptable piles: piles not meeting load capacity, volume factor, or structural integrity requirements must be assessed by the engineer for acceptance, supplemental piles, or replacement.
key_points: Grout/concrete placement within 5 minutes of reaching tip depth
Volume factor must stay within 7.5% of target from approved installation plan
Adjacent piles within 6D: must wait for first pile to attain sufficient strength before installing neighbors
Automated monitoring every 2 ft (0.6 m): tip depth, volume, pressure — all referenced to auger tip depth
Integrity testing: minimum 20% of production piles (SE, IR, CSL, or gamma-gamma)
Pile position tolerance: center within 75 mm (3 in.) of plan location; plumb per spec
Non-metallic spacers only; cover 75 mm standard, 100 mm for aggressive environments
